Outputs: the eligible path updates timing state; the ineligible path returns to the caller's caller. Assumptions: the routine is entered only through the expected JSR stack frame. Clobbers: A, flags, timing state, and two stack bytes on the abort path. Hardware changes: none.

16 event-indexed minimum intervals. $A4CB subtracts the last per-event tick $0268,X from current $E2, compares to this table and discards the caller return frame when too soon; accepted events update the saved tick. Most intervals are 1, with exceptions 6,2 and4 in the captured table.

Purpose: translate the normalized Central Park input byte and current player state into facing, movement, pose, action, and animation requests
Inputs: normalized active-low/control byte $7C; death/condition latch $B6; player state $61,$65,$68/$69,$6C/$6D,$70,$89; decode tables beginning at $A69C
Outputs: updates desired direction $68, facing $69, action/motion $6C/$6D, pose $65, dirty flag $9F, and may select/install a player animation
Assumptions: an earlier input service has populated $7C and the control/animation tables are resident
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-control/animation scratch
Hardware changes: none; no CIA register is read or written here

Continuation of $A4CB control interpretation: applies desired heading $68, allowing odd headings to replace $69 except an exact opposite; marks redraw $9F when changed. Sets movement $6C and derives facing/pose $65 and $6D. The $A567 idle path clears $02B8 and may select an idle animation; $A591 onward handles changes in the fire/action state $78, comparing direction to facing before selecting an action through $A600. Uses $A638 and $A69C direction lookups; no direct hardware writes. Entry is within the larger control routine, not an independent callable API.

Purpose: Translate action code A into the Central Park playable phase's player animation pointer and install that animation.
Inputs: A is the action code selected by control/AI logic; $69 is player facing; phase animation lookup tables are valid.
Outputs: Stores A in $60, derives the facing-adjusted animation index, loads its pointer, initializes $60/$61/$5C/$58/$96/$5D, and returns.
Assumptions: A is one of the action codes represented by the phase animation tables.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $58, $5C/$5D, $60/$61, $6D, and $96.
Hardware changes: No direct hardware-register writes.

Purpose: install a new player animation-bytecode stream and prime its first control byte
Inputs: X = stream low byte; A = stream high byte; desired direction $68 and facing $69
Outputs: stores the stream pointer in $60/$61, loads its first byte into $5C, clears animation delay $58, copies $68 to $96, and stores $69 bit 1 in $5D
Assumptions: A:X addresses a valid animation stream whose first byte is readable
Clobbers: A, Y, and flags; X is preserved
Hardware changes: none

Eight action-heading values 1,7,1,7,5,3,5,3 selected at $A5EE. Index combines desired cardinal direction and current facing, then output replaces desired heading $68 before action animation selection. This is separate from the joystick low-nibble map $A69C.

Purpose: Interpret the Central Park playable phase's normalized control latch and update player motion/action animation state.
Inputs: $7C is the resident-normalized control byte; player animation, action, timing, facing, and collision state are current.
Outputs: Maps the low control nybble through the phase action table, updates movement/action timers and facing, and selects an animation when state changes.
Assumptions: This entry consumes $7C; it does not read CIA joystick registers directly.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, player input/action/timing/facing fields, and animation-installation state on paths that select a new animation.
Hardware changes: No direct CIA or other hardware-register writes.

Eight alternating delays 4,8 indexed by normalized direction Y. $A66D compares elapsed tick difference against the chosen threshold before deriving action code $84*4+8 and selecting animation. This table controls action timing, not the joystick direction conversion.

16-entry map of the low four normalized control bits to eight directions 0..7 or $FF for no valid direction. $A507, $A5B5 and $A645 use it to choose movement/facing/action; opposing direction combinations map to $FF. Fire occupies a different input bit and is handled separately.

High-byte indexed alias of the little-endian pointer/row directory starting at $A6AC. The consumer doubles its logical index before the paired reads; no separate high-byte allocation begins here. The owning directory describes its full extent.

18 packed lookup bytes used at $A609 after deriving action class A>>2 and facing. The selected offset is combined with facing to index the absolute animation pointer directory at $A6AC. Values include $0C,$04,$18,$10,$1C,$14,$20,$28; they are byte offsets, not frame numbers.

Purpose: build, advance, validate, and commit the player's movement candidate for this tick
Inputs: player position/extents $54/$55,$50/$51; enemy position $56/$57; desired direction $68; facing $69; elapsed steps $8F; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: initializes candidate $48-$4D and opposing position $C9/$CA, calls CentralParkAdvanceCandidate, commits candidate position/extents back to $54/$55,$50/$51, and reports vertical displacement through the shared tail at $A7C9 with X=0
Assumptions: movement and compiled collision data are initialized and facing indexes the movement profile
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: build and advance the enemy movement candidate, record collision outcomes, and commit it only inside the playable bounds
Inputs: enemy position/extents $56/$57,$52/$53; player position $54/$55; desired direction $6A; facing $6B; elapsed steps $8F; profile selector $D3; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: updates candidate/collision scratch; records collision in $02B0/$02B2/$02B4 or failure count $02B1; commits $56/$57,$52/$53 only for X in [$02,$F6] and Y in [$09,$BC]; reports vertical displacement through $A7C9 with X=2
Assumptions: movement profiles and compiled collision records are resident and initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA,$CD
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: apply a signed vertical or height delta to an actor with saturation. Inputs: A is the signed delta and X is the actor offset. Outputs: $74,X is updated within its limits or left unchanged when inactive or inhibited. Assumptions: X uses the engine's actor stride. Clobbers: A, flags, and $74,X; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: run the enemy animation interpreter once when the IRQ tick has advanced
Inputs: current tick $E2, enemy animation stamp $026E, and the already-installed enemy animation stream/state at actor offset 2
Outputs: if no tick elapsed, returns unchanged; otherwise stores elapsed delta in $8F, stamps $026E, sets X=2, and tail-enters the shared animation interpreter
Assumptions: IRQ tick advances and the enemy animation state is already installed and valid
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $8F, $026E, and all animation-interpreter scratch/state on the admitted path
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: interpret one elapsed step of the selected actor's animation bytecode, including delay, pose, coordinate deltas, event generation, and continuation
Inputs: X=0 at $A802 for player or X=2 at $A804 for enemy; pointer $60/$61,X; control/delay $5C/$58-$59,X; actor position $54/$55,X; elapsed ticks $8F
Outputs: advances delay and stream position, updates pose $65,X, position $54/$55,X, event $64,X, continuation pointer, movement flags, and recomposes the actor's logical sprites when required
Assumptions: X is 0 or 2 and the installed bytecode stream is valid
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and animation, movement, event, collision, and sprite-composition scratch
Hardware changes: none directly; updates logical sprite RAM consumed by the raster path

Purpose: Run the Central Park playable phase's animation interpreter for the scheduled enemy slot.
Inputs: X is the enemy animation-state offset selected by the scheduler (normally 2); $61,X is its stream pointer high byte; timing and animation state are current.
Outputs: Honors animation delay, decodes one bytecode step when due, updates the enemy animation/movement/event state, composes the resulting actor frame when requested, and returns.
Assumptions: The enemy animation pointer is zero or addresses a valid phase animation stream.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02/$03, animation timing/pointer/state bytes for slot X, actor-frame/sprite scratch, and event state selected by the bytecode.
Hardware changes: No direct hardware-register writes; bytecode paths requesting composition alter sprite work buffers and change CPU-port banking transiently before restoring it.

Purpose: compose an actor's current frame and test its scene interactions. Inputs: X actor offset and current animation frame. Outputs: sprite buffers and condition state are updated and X is restored. Assumptions: actor frame data is valid. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and shared renderer scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite or image RAM only directly.

Purpose: Return immediately from the Central Park playable phase's animation interpreter on the shared no-further-work path.
Inputs: The preceding animation branch has completed or determined that no frame composition is needed.
Outputs: Returns to the interpreter's caller without additional state or hardware changes.
Assumptions: A valid JSR return address is on the stack.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: delay for the requested number of engine ticks. Inputs: A is the tick count. Outputs: the requested tick transitions have elapsed. Assumptions: an interrupt or service updates $E2. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and wait scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: advance an actor candidate by up to eight elapsed substeps and test each proposed segment against compiled collision geometry
Inputs: X = heading/quadrant selector; Y = movement-profile selector; old/candidate position $48-$4B; candidate extents $4C/$4D; direction mask $1E; elapsed count $8F
Outputs: stores profile in $027F and capped count in $8E; updates candidate coordinates; returns collision and trigger state through $23/$24,$80/$81,$CD and related movement scratch
Assumptions: direction/profile tables and compiled collision records are resident; $8F may exceed eight but only eight substeps are admitted
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and broad candidate/collision scratch
Hardware changes: none

Four negative-X entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Four positive-X entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Four negative-Y entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Four positive-Y entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Four vertical guard entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Four horizontal guard entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Four contact direction entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Four contact flip entries, read by the movement-candidate logic at $A48C/$A906-$A9B6 with its direction/profile index. Bitwise AND against the movement mask selects eligible axis/guard paths; $AA21 supplies zero or $FF for contact handling. Each four-byte group has a distinct consumer role.

Purpose: consume and dispatch pending player and enemy animation events through the shared target-minus-one event table
Inputs: player event $64 and enemy event $66; event table begins at $AA4B; X=0 selects player and X=2 enemy
Outputs: dispatches each nonzero event through the RTS table, clears $64 after the player handler and $66 after the enemy handler, and returns after both channels are empty
Assumptions: nonzero event codes index valid target-minus-one entries and handlers return to the dispatcher
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, two stack bytes per dispatch, and handler-dependent state
Hardware changes: none in the dispatcher; handler-dependent afterward

Purpose: dispatch an event handler through a target-minus-one RTS table. Inputs: A is the event index. Outputs: control transfers to the selected handler, which returns to the original caller. Assumptions: the table entry is valid and the stack has room. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and two transient stack bytes. Hardware changes: none.

24 little-endian event-handler-minus-one words at $AA4B-$AA7A. $AA40 doubles the event, pushes high then low, and RTS dispatches to word+1. Several slots select $AA7C, and zero selects the no-op $AA7B, although the outer dispatcher skips zero events. Both player and enemy channels use this table.
Odd-byte indexed base of the event directory at $AA4B, read at $AA42 with Y=2*event. This byte is the high byte of slot zero; the directory has 24 words, not a separate high-byte array.

Purpose: Consume an event-table slot without performing an action.
Inputs: Actor selector X and event index are ignored.
Outputs: Returns immediately; the outer dispatcher subsequently clears the consumed event byte.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: No registers or flags; RTS consumes the dispatcher-supplied return address.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: If command bit 0 is armed and the actor mode is not $0C, move player X by -4, increment player Y, update movement, and mark redraw state.
Inputs: Command flags $81, player X/Y $54/$55, actor mode $6D, and actor selector X supplied by event dispatch.
Outputs: Eligible path adds signed -4 to $54, increments $55, calls movement helper $A7C9 with A=1/X=0, and writes $9F=$FF; rejected paths return unchanged.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $54, $55, movement scratch, and $9F.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: If command bit 0 is armed and the actor mode is not $0C, move player X by +4, increment player Y, update movement, and mark redraw state.
Inputs: Command flags $81, player X/Y $54/$55, actor mode $6D, and actor selector X supplied by event dispatch.
Outputs: Eligible path adds signed 4 to $54, increments $55, calls movement helper $A7C9 with A=1/X=0, and writes $9F=$FF; rejected paths return unchanged.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $54, $55, movement scratch, and $9F.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Copy state byte $89 into actor-state byte $70 for two event codes.
Inputs: $89.
Outputs: Writes $70=$89 and returns with A equal to the copied value.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A and flags; $70.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Handle event 3 differently for the player channel and opponent channel.
Inputs: Actor selector X from event dispatch and current animation/AI state.
Outputs: For X=0, calls $A8F1 with A=$14, waits through $11F1, and sets $B4=$FF; for X!=0, sets opponent AI state $CF=$0B.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, animation/pacing scratch, and either $B4 or $CF.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Apply $2C units of player damage for event $0D.
Inputs: Player energy $0229 and existing death state.
Outputs: Tail-calls CentralParkDamagePlayer with A=$2C.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, flags, player energy $0229, death latch $B6, and combat scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Randomly perturb three paired level-data coordinates, move the opponent two units toward the player on each axis, and damage the player on close overlap.
Inputs: Random source $B51F, coordinate pairs at $CE49/$CE4A for X offsets 8/4/0, player position $54/$55, and opponent position $56/$57.
Outputs: Keeps each data perturbation inside its encoded eight-value range, adjusts $56/$57 by two toward $54/$55, and calls player damage with A=1 when absolute X<8 and absolute Y<10.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, scratch $1E, $CE49/$CE4A records, opponent coordinates $56/$57, and possibly player energy/death state.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: test the combat overlap mode and apply the selected actor-to-actor hit, damage, score, and reaction result
Inputs: X = attacking actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy); this semantic entry sets overlap mode Y=3; actor geometry/state; reaction bytes $6C-$6F; damage tables $ABA6/$ABBA
Outputs: on overlap, ignores a target already in reaction $24, otherwise selects damage, calls DamagePlayer or DamageEnemy, awards score on the player-hit path, and latches the opposing actor's reaction
Assumptions: actor extents and combat tables are initialized; generated alternate entries may supply modes 4-6 separately
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and overlap/damage/score scratch
Hardware changes: none directly; score, UI, or audio-facing state may change through callees

Purpose: resolve the selected combat-contact event. Inputs: actor state and the contact type selected by the entry path. Outputs: damage, reaction animation, collision, and object state are updated. Assumptions: actor slots and contact flags are coherent. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and combat scratch. Hardware changes: may change presentation or audio indirectly through damage and animation helpers.

Purpose: Resolve actor overlap using combat profile 5 and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X, both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $AD46-$AD85.
Outputs: Loads Y=5, runs the shared overlap query, and on a hit applies profile-derived damage to the selected actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, and possible death/defeat persistence.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Resolve actor overlap using combat profile 6 and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X, both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $AD46-$AD85.
Outputs: Loads Y=6, runs the shared overlap query, and on a hit applies profile-derived damage to the selected actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, and possible death/defeat persistence.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Resolve the Central Park playable phase's confirmed combat overlap for actor slot X, selecting the player or opponent reaction path.
Inputs: X selects actor slot 0 or the opponent slot; overlap geometry and combat state were established by the caller.
Outputs: Branches on X, applies the matching hit/reaction/damage logic, updates actor/combat state, and returns its path result.
Assumptions: Entered only after the caller's overlap test succeeded.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, combat/reaction scratch, and the affected actor's health/action state.
Hardware changes: No direct hardware-register writes.

Purpose: Resolve combat overlap using the profile derived from the selected actor's current mode, then dispatch damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X plus both actors' positions, headings, animation modes, energies, and collision profile tables.
Outputs: Runs $AC7A to derive the active profile and overlap result; on a hit applies actor-specific damage and reaction animation.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, and possible death/defeat persistence.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

20 encoded attack strengths read at $AB88 for an enemy attack against the player. Index $1F combines attack-pose class and weapon state; result enters the independently checked saturating player-damage routine $B54A. The last four values form a retained tail of this lookup; the engine index bounds remain to be exercised.

16 attack values read at $AB91/$AB97 for player attacks, passed both to score accounting $1187 and enemy-meter handler $B568. That handler compares against a tick-regenerated meter and clears it; it is not conventional cumulative health subtraction. Exact player-visible combat outcome is still open pending live cases.

Purpose: select and install the victim's hit-reaction animation. Inputs: attacker and victim orientation plus actor state. Outputs: reaction animation is installed and the consumed hit flag is cleared. Assumptions: reaction tables match the engine facing encoding. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state. Hardware changes: none directly.

32 little-endian animation/script pointers at $AC3A-$AC79. $AC01/$AC10 and their paired high reads select one using facing/contact state and install it through $AD3B. Targets are valid streams in the checked $C2C4-$C4C1 pool; table stores absolute pointers, unlike the event RTS directory.
High-byte base of the interleaved pointer table $AC3A, read with even Y by $AC04/$AC13. The physical table holds 32 two-byte entries through $AC79.

Purpose: test whether the selected combat actors overlap. Inputs: X selects an actor and current positions and bounds are valid. Outputs: flags and transient contact state report overlap or separation. Assumptions: actor layout and bounds tables are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and overlap scratch. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: mark AI scripting active and install a new AI script pointer. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $76 is set to one, $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Assumptions: the pointer addresses a valid AI stream in the active phase. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: install an AI script without changing the active marker. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Assumptions: the pointer addresses a valid AI stream in the active phase. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Finish installing a Central Park AI script when its low pointer byte was stored separately. Inputs: A is the script-pointer high byte and $62 already contains its low byte. Outputs: $63 receives A, $5E and $5A are cleared, and A returns zero; $62 is unchanged. Assumptions: $62/A forms a valid script pointer in the active Central Park playable occupant. Clobbers: A, N, Z, $63, $5E, and $5A; X, Y, C, V, and $62 are preserved. Hardware changes: None; only AI-script RAM state is written.

16 unsigned lower horizontal bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper horizontal bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 unsigned lower vertical bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper vertical bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

Purpose: Restore an actor's saved mode, derive its facing/pose code, and perform channel-specific follow-up.
Inputs: Actor channel offset X, current heading/mode at $69+X, saved mode at $71+X, and actor state arrays $5D/$65.
Outputs: Copies heading bit 1 to $5D+X, restores $6D+X from $71+X, derives $65+X from restored/current heading; player channel sets $9F=$FF, opponent channel rebuilds state and sets $CF=8.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $5D+X/$6D+X/$65+X, and either $9F or opponent helper/AI state.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: admit and dispatch one active-opponent AI step, or route collision/boundary state to recovery
Inputs: active-enemy sign latch $CB; collision/boundary fields $02B0-$02B2; AI state $CF; timer slot 12; target-minus-one table beginning at $ADEA
Outputs: inactive enemies return; collision/boundary state jumps to recovery at $B11E; admitted normal state dispatches the selected AI handler by stack/RTS
Assumptions: negative $CB means an active enemy, timer service is initialized, and $CF indexes a valid AI target
Clobbers: A, X, flags, two stack bytes, and handler-dependent state; Y is preserved until the handler
Hardware changes: none in the dispatcher

16 target-minus-one words $ADEA-$AE09 selected by twice AI state $CF. $ADDE/$ADE2 push high/low and RTS transfers to word+1. Slot 14 stores $FFFF and would wrap to zero, so table length is not evidence that every state is reachable or safe.
High-byte indexed alias of the 16-word AI RTS directory at $ADEA; even X comes from twice $CF. Keep the $FFFF slot visible as an unresolved state case.

Purpose: Update derived opponent heading byte $6F by blending current heading $6B with target value 4.
Inputs: Current opponent heading $6B.
Outputs: Stores floor(($6B + 8)/2) in $6F and returns.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A and flags; $6F.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Blend the Central Park playable phase's current opponent heading toward zero through the common heading-average tail.
Inputs: $6B is the current opponent heading/direction code.
Outputs: Computes $6F=(2*0+$6B)/2 and returns with the blended heading stored in $6F.
Assumptions: The heading values use the phase's unsigned direction encoding.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, and $6F; X and Y are preserved.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: smooth an AI desired direction against its current facing. Inputs: A is desired direction and $6B is current direction. Outputs: the blended direction or state is written to $6F. Assumptions: direction values use the engine's cyclic encoding. Clobbers: A, flags, and $6F. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Initialize a timed AI decision state and its random delay.
Inputs: AI option byte $D0 bit 6, tick $E2, current heading $6B, and random source $B51F.
Outputs: Sets state $CF to 3 or 4, snapshots tick to $0275, stores random delay 0..31 in $CC, and updates $6F with the zero-target heading blend.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0275, $CC, $6F, and random-source scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Wait for the AI delay to expire, then enter state 5 with a rebuilt heading/action.
Inputs: Current tick $E2, delay origin $0275, delay $CC, current heading $6B, and helper state.
Outputs: Before expiry returns unchanged; at expiry sets $CF=5, derives and stores a new heading in $6A/$6B, invokes setup $B346 with X=8, and updates $6F using target 8.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Face the opponent into the player's current relative quadrant and enter approach state 5. Despite the historical name this entry is fully deterministic.
Inputs: Player high-byte coordinates $54/$55 and opponent high-byte coordinates $56/$57; opponent heading and action fields.
Outputs: Sets AI state $CF=5, stores the quadrant classification returned by $B32E into both $6B (current heading) and $6A (desired heading), installs direction action class 8 through $B346 with X=8, blends the heading value toward 8 into $6F through $AE10, and returns.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active and actor coordinates use the verified 8.8 high-byte encoding.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $6A/$6B/$6F/$CF and helper scratch; Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: None. No PRNG call occurs here, so CIA 1 Timer A registers $DC04/$DC05 and PRNG state $F9-$FB are not touched.

Purpose: After the timed delay, choose a two-step heading turn, enter state 2, and begin horizontal-travel tracking.
Inputs: Tick/delay fields $E2/$0275/$CC, random source, heading $6B, and opponent X $56.
Outputs: At expiry sets $CF=2, rotates $6A/$6B by +2 or -2 modulo 8, snapshots $56 in $D1, runs setup X=$18 and heading blend target 8, then continues into the travel tracker at $AE81.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, $D1, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Track horizontal displacement from $D1, escalate after at least $14 units, and fall back to state 5 when the range test drops below $70.
Inputs: Opponent heading $6B, current X $56, baseline X $D1, tick $E2, and distance helper $B30C.
Outputs: At sufficient directed displacement sets $CF=$0C, snapshots tick, calls setup X=4, and updates heading blend toward zero; independently, a helper result below $70 resets through the state-5 entry.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $CF, $0275, $6F, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Every 12 ticks, enter state $0F, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275, heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 12 ticks returns; afterward updates $0275, sets $CF=$0F, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=4, and updates $6F toward zero.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $0275, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Every 6 ticks, enter state 2, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275, heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 6 ticks returns; afterward sets $CF=2, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=$18, and updates $6F toward target 8.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Navigate the opponent relative to the player and collision geometry, selecting movement, reset, or attack states from distance and heading tests.
Inputs: Player/opponent positions $54/$55/$56/$57, headings $68/$6A/$6B, behavior fields $CB/$72, saved coordinates $028A/$028B/$028E/$028F, tick $E2, and collision/distance helpers $B30C/$B30E/$B32E/$B330/$B346.
Outputs: Clamps/wraps candidate coordinates, may restore the saved player position and enter state 6, may enter state 9 after a distance comparison, otherwise updates desired/current opponent heading and setup state; several rejection paths reset through state 5.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $1D-$21, $54/$56, $6A/$6B/$6F, $CF, $028A/$028B/$028E/$028F/$02BE, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Retarget the Central Park playable phase's opponent AI to the player's current coordinates.
Inputs: Player coordinates are $54/$55; opponent target/heading state and the phase PRNG are initialized.
Outputs: Copies $54/$55 to $028A/$028B, chooses a random heading into $6A/$6B, applies the heading helper, blends toward zero into $6F, sets $CF=6, and returns.
Assumptions: Player coordinates are valid in the phase's wrapped map coordinate system.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, PRNG state $F9-$FB, helper scratch, $028A/$028B, $6A/$6B/$6F, and $CF; Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: No hardware registers are written; each PRNG call reads CIA 1 Timer A low at $DC04 and reads high at $DC05 only on reseeding.

Purpose: Choose between an immediate recovery/timer state and a randomized attack setup from the player's current actor mode.
Inputs: Player actor mode $6D, behavior selector $72, tick $E2, random source, opponent heading $6B, and AI sequence counter $02BD.
Outputs: If ($6D&$FC)==$24, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5; otherwise selects a bounded random action/setup, sets $CF=7, and increments $02BD.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, $6F, $02BD, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Choose and install a random close-range opponent action for the Central Park playable phase.
Inputs: Opponent/player proximity tests have reached the close-range branch; orientation $72, animation state, and PRNG are current.
Outputs: Selects a bounded random variant, installs its animation/heading parameters through the phase helpers, sets $CF=7, increments $02BD, and returns.
Assumptions: The selected random value indexes the verified close-range action table.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, PRNG state $F9-$FB, helper scratch, action/animation state, $CF, and $02BD; Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: No hardware registers are written; each PRNG call reads CIA 1 Timer A low at $DC04 and reads high at $DC05 only on reseeding.

Purpose: Wait for the opponent animation pointer high byte to clear, then initialize AI state 8 timing.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63, tick $E2, and random source.
Outputs: Returns while $63 is nonzero; when zero, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, and random-source scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: decide whether the player is close enough to the AI target for a scripted action. Inputs: player coordinates, $028A/$028B target coordinates, and AI state and timers. Outputs: proximity and action state are updated and an AI path may be entered. Assumptions: target coordinates are initialized. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI scratch. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Wait for both opponent animation completion and projectile slot 1 inactivity, then reset through AI state 5.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63 and projectile slot-1 state $0281.
Outputs: Returns if either field is nonzero; when both are zero, tail-enters the state-5 reset at $AE3A.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, flags, and on reset A/X plus $CF/$6A/$6B/$6F and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Return immediately for the intentionally inactive AI state-table entry.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: Returns through the stored-return dispatcher without changing registers, flags, RAM, or hardware.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: No registers or flags; RTS consumes the dispatcher-supplied return address.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Test the current area's persistent opponent record for subtype $2C and, when its spatial conditions apply, consume its high flag and start AI state 7 with a heading-selected animation.
Inputs: Area index $A2, persistent status array $012D+, player/opponent positions $54-$57, heading $6B, and animation pointers $C3ED/$C3E3.
Outputs: On a qualifying record, clears status bit 7, sets $CF=7, installs one of two animations according to heading bit 2, and writes $0236=6; otherwise returns without transition.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, selected $012D+ status, $CF, enemy animation state $5A/$5E/$62/$63, and $0236.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: Consume the Central Park playable phase's pending opponent target identifier and update the AI target history/state.
Inputs: $02B0 is the pending target ID or $FF; $02B3/$02A4/$02A5 and opponent AI state are current.
Outputs: Reads then clears $02B0 to $FF, ignores the sentinel, otherwise rotates target history as needed and dispatches the matching target/approach behavior.
Assumptions: Target IDs use the verified phase object/actor encoding.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02B0, $02B3/$02A4/$02A5, and AI action/target scratch on non-sentinel paths.
Hardware changes: No direct hardware-register writes.

Purpose: Validate the selected collision-record index against the opponent's X position and either reset the selection, resume navigation, or continue heading/distance analysis.
Inputs: Selected record index $02B3, collision-record coordinate arrays $FEF9/$FEFB indexed by X, opponent position $56/$57, player position $54/$55, and current heading $6B.
Outputs: Clears $02B3 and resets to state 5 when the record is absent/out of range; may resume navigation at $AF42 for near conditions; otherwise derives a heading/distance decision and continues through the shared AI tail.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $02B3, $1C-$21, $6A/$6B, $CF, and helper scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Purpose: choose enemy facing and action from contact geometry. Inputs: A is desired input, X is the contact selector or sentinel, and actor positions are valid. Outputs: $6A/$6B facing state and possibly the AI script are updated. Assumptions: direction and action tables match the current phase. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI state. Hardware changes: none.

16 direction-selection bytes read at $B29F after doubling contact selector $1E and incorporating compiled-record bit $40. Nonnegative result becomes desired heading $6A; a negative entry takes the visible red-border trap loop $B2A7. The trap is traced; reachable contact combinations still require ordinary-input checks.

64 contact-geometry direction entries, $B2BD-$B2FC. $B24F combines flags and selector state into Y, then $B252 loads this table; negative entries take the trap, otherwise heading may be reversed and stored in $6A/$6B. A direction map for collision/AI decisions, not sprite selectors.

Seven distance offsets read at $AF2A/$AF34 using the enemy profile $72. Added to or subtracted from player X to decide opponent approach. The following heading-map base starts at $B304; profile bounds outside these seven values are not assumed.

Eight heading mappings read at $B02E after comparing near-contact horizontal/vertical separation. The resulting direction is stored in $6A; the table ends at $B30B before the Manhattan-distance routine.

Purpose: compute Manhattan distance between the engine's two coordinate pairs. Inputs: $54/$55 and $56/$57 are the two coordinate pairs. Outputs: $1C and $1D receive the absolute horizontal and vertical deltas; A is their sum saturated at $FF. Assumptions: coordinates use unsigned eight-bit axes. Clobbers: A, flags, $1C, and $1D; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: compute saturated Manhattan distance with the first X coordinate supplied by the caller. Inputs: A is first X and $55-$57 hold the remaining coordinates. Outputs: $1C and $1D receive the absolute horizontal and vertical deltas; A is their sum saturated at $FF. Assumptions: the caller intentionally bypasses the wrapper's $54 load. Clobbers: A, flags, $1C, and $1D; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: classify the second coordinate pair's quadrant relative to the first. Inputs: $54-$57 contain the two coordinate pairs. Outputs: A is the phase-table quadrant/direction code and $1F contains transient horizontal comparison state. Assumptions: coordinate equality follows the observed comparison branches. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and $1F; Y is preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: classify relative quadrant with the first X coordinate supplied in A. Inputs: A is first X and $55-$57 hold the remaining coordinates. Outputs: A is the phase-table quadrant/direction code and $1F contains transient horizontal comparison state. Assumptions: the caller intentionally bypasses the wrapper's $54 load. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and $1F; Y is preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: select and install the AI action matching direction and action class. Inputs: A is direction or facing and X is the action-table offset. Outputs: AI pointer, first opcode or state, and script index are initialized. Assumptions: Central Park action table and selected stream are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI script state. Hardware changes: none.
Four action delays 8,6,4,4 indexed by $D3 at $B358 and written to animation/state countdown $5B before an AI action is installed.

26 little-endian action/animation pointers through $B3A9. $B346 derives an even table offset from facing/action class, reads low/high via $B376/$B377 and installs $62/$63 with its first opcode at $5E. Targets include the main $C2C4 animation pool and four small retained streams beginning $B3AA.
High-byte indexed base of the action pointer table beginning $B376; X is an even offset. The table ends before retained action-stream bytes at $B3AA.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3AA-$B3AD. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3AE-$B3B1. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3B2-$B3C3. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3C4-$B3D5. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Rebuild the current area enemy meter from the 16-bit tick pair $F0:$E2 and saved tick origin $0187,X:$0175,X. Computes delta modulo 65536, shifts right five, subtracts two with a zero floor and clamps to 44. Writes both $022A and $3F92,X. Sixteen native boundary/wrap cases matched this formula. The inputs are elapsed ticks, not world-height coordinates; X is current area $A2.

Purpose: draw a phase-local UI or status image record. Inputs: A is image index and X is placement variant. Outputs: the selected UI image is rendered. Assumptions: the image-table entry and renderer workspace are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02-$05, and renderer scratch. Hardware changes: reads VIC-II control state at $D011 and changes hardware-visible bitmap, screen, and color RAM.

Purpose: dissolve and erase the display strip at $0C00-$0FFF. Inputs: current strip contents and pseudo-random state. Outputs: several masked dissolve passes are displayed and the region is finally cleared. Assumptions: the range is the intended visible region under the current VIC-II layout. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and random and delay scratch. Hardware changes: changes hardware-visible bitmap or screen RAM; no direct VIC-II register write.

Purpose: Advance and return Central Park's table- and CIA-timer-mixed pseudo-random byte. Inputs: $F9/$FA is the readable table pointer, $FB is the previous random byte, Y is caller state to preserve, and CIA 1 Timer A is running at $DC04/$DC05. Outputs: If old $FA is at least $CE, sets $FA=($DC04 & $1F)+$8A and $F9=$DC05. Then A and $FB receive old $FB + byte[$F9/$FA] + $DC04 modulo 256; $F9 increments and $FA increments on low-byte wrap; Y is restored. Assumptions: $F9/$FA points at readable mapped data. Both paths establish carry clear before the two ADC operations, and the caller accepts CIA-timer-dependent output. Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, V, and $F9-$FB; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: Reads CIA 1 Timer A low byte $DC04 on every call and high byte $DC05 only on reseed; performs no hardware write.

Subtract unsigned A from player health $0229 with saturation at zero. Positive remaining health preserves action $6D and death latch $B6. Only the zero-result path sets $6D=($69>>1)+$24 and $B6=$FF. X/Y are preserved; no hardware registers are written. Live tests cover positive, equal, excessive and zero damage, including health 0 and 255.

Purpose: subtract one hit from enemy health, update its HUD value, and on defeat persist position/time state and award score
Inputs: A = unsigned damage; enemy health $022A; current area $A2; enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B; tick/time state; defeated-count limit $D6
Outputs: stores saturated health in $022A and HUD cell $3F92,$A2; on defeat awards score, records position/heading/time in $013F/$0151/$0163/$0175/$0187 indexed by area, advances bounded persistent state $012D,X, and installs reaction/action $24
Assumptions: area-indexed persistent arrays and resident score helper are valid
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and score/persistence/reaction scratch
Hardware changes: none directly; HUD and score display state change through RAM/helpers

Purpose: create the current area's enemy from static spawn tables or restore its persistent defeated/position record
Inputs: area index $A2; spawn/profile tables $B67F,$B691,$B6A3,$B6B5,$B6C7; persistent state $012D/$013F/$0151/$0163; related enemy profile fields
Outputs: initializes enemy script/motion, extents, delay, AI state, type/attributes, position, heading, action and timing fields; a zero spawn Y disables the enemy; otherwise composes its initial logical sprites
Assumptions: area indexes all parallel tables and negative $012D,X denotes the persistent restore path
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and enemy/script/sprite-composition state
Hardware changes: none directly; logical sprite RAM is prepared for later raster output

Eight pose entries read at $B64A. Y is half the selected enemy heading on the ordinary path and an adjusted heading on the preserved-enemy path; result goes to $67. The table is separate from the area-indexed enemy fields.

Eight mirror/auxiliary flags read at $B64F using the same heading-derived Y as $B66F; writes $5F. Values are zero or $FF; the exact visual effect is traced by the frame composer, not inferred from the flag name.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B67F-$B690: upper nibble selects $7F, lower nibble $72; lower nibble with bit 7 sets $CB. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B691-$B6A2: initial enemy X written to $56. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B6A3-$B6B4: initial enemy Y written to $57/$76; zero takes the no-spawn path. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B6B5-$B6C6: low three bits set heading $6B; upper nibble sets $D6. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B6C7-$B6D8: sets $D0, with low two bits copied to $D3. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

Purpose: spawn the attacking actor's projectile into its fixed player or enemy slot after the combat-overlap precheck
Inputs: X = source actor offset (0 player, nonzero enemy); actor position/facing $54-$57/$69/$6B; player selected-object state $70/$0279/$03DC; projectile arrays $0280-$0289
Outputs: player attacks populate slot 0 only when free and allowed by selected-object state; enemy attacks populate slot 1; position, direction, lifetime, and collision stamps are initialized
Assumptions: two projectile slots are encoded at adjacent indices and actor coordinates/headings are initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and combat-overlap/projectile initialization scratch
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: initialize the single projectile slot when it is free. Inputs: A is projectile kind or state and actor and facing context are valid. Outputs: projectile owner, direction, coordinates, and state are initialized or left unchanged when occupied. Assumptions: the engine uses one active projectile slot. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and projectile state. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: test a projectile/actor pair against the engine's two-axis collision box. Inputs: X selects projectile coordinates $0284,X/$0286,X; Y selects actor coordinates $54,Y/$55,Y. Outputs: carry is clear exactly when absolute vertical distance is below 8 and absolute horizontal distance is below 6; carry is set on either rejection. Assumptions: the caller consumes carry immediately and X/Y select valid slots. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: initialize a projectile trajectory from an actor. Inputs: projectile type, source actor, facing, and coordinates. Outputs: projectile owner, state, origin, direction, and signed velocity are installed. Assumptions: the projectile slot has already been accepted. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and projectile state. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: advance both projectile slots for elapsed IRQ ticks and remove or resolve projectiles that expire, leave bounds, hit geometry, or overlap an actor
Inputs: tick $E2/$0273; two projectile slots in $0280-$0289; compiled collision geometry and actor positions/extents/health
Outputs: stamps elapsed delta in $8F/$0273; advances lifetime and coordinates for slots 1 then 0; clears expired/hit slots and applies damage/reaction on actor overlap
Assumptions: IRQ tick advances, projectile arrays use the verified adjacent-slot layout, and collision/actor state is initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and projectile, collision, overlap, damage, and reaction scratch
Hardware changes: none directly; updates logical state rendered later

Projectile-state indexed graphic field, read at $BCE6/$BCEF. When paired high byte $B8FA is nonzero, forms $06/$07 pointing at packed sprite bytes ($FBE0 or $FCE0 for the relevant states). With high zero, this byte is a sprite selector passed through $BF1E. $BC D0 toggles state bit 3 before the lookup; the same values therefore alternate projectile image phase.

Indexed high byte paired with $B8EA: nonzero uses a direct source pointer; zero chooses the packed-sprite directory through the low field. Entries with $FB/$FC point into the retained raw/high graphics bank. Ordinary projectile-state bounds remain a separate verification question.

Projectile-state indexed logical-sprite attribute byte read at $BCD9 and stored to $0220,X. $FF and values 1/6 are retained literally. It supplies display attributes; the adjacent offset maps at $B919/$B920 serve position adjustment instead.

Projectile direction-indexed signed X offsets. $BD0B masks projectile state to three bits, adds this field to the world coordinate and writes staged logical-sprite position. The eight-entry indexed window may overlap the neighboring table byte; bounds are the consumer index, not a guessed padding rule.

Projectile direction-indexed signed Y offsets. $BD0B masks projectile state to three bits, adds this field to the world coordinate and writes staged logical-sprite position. The eight-entry indexed window may overlap the neighboring table byte; bounds are the consumer index, not a guessed padding rule.

Indexed X-offset base read at $B742/$B794 using actor heading X. Added to enemy/player X with explicit overflow rejection before storing projectile X. Paired Y-offset reads use the overlapping base $B928, so these bases must not be described as disjoint eight-byte arrays.
Indexed Y spawn-offset base at $B758/$B7AA, read using actor heading X and added to enemy/player Y. Overlaps the X-offset base $B927. This is spawn positioning, not a movement increment lookup.

X movement-increment base read at $B844. Y combines projectile heading and a projectile-kind offset from $B948; negative X increments take a borrow-check path, while positive increments take a carry-check path before writing $0284,X. The neighboring $B930 base supplies Y movement, so the bytes are indexed coordinate pairs rather than a separate eight-byte Y table.

Y movement increments read at $B85E with the same combined index as the $B92F X increments. Adds to $0286,X, then rejects coordinates below $22 or at least $B1. Indexed bases overlap; consumer index domains are not guessed from adjacent labels.

Physical continuation bytes in the indexed projectile-motion parameter pool beginning $B92F/$B930. Effective reads are formed by adding heading and kind offset; no instruction directly addresses $B936. This is not a separate spawn-offset table, and its values retain the motion-pool context.

Physical continuation bytes in the indexed projectile-motion parameter pool beginning $B92F/$B930. Effective reads are formed by adding heading and kind offset; no instruction directly addresses $B93D. This is not a separate spawn-offset table, and its values retain the motion-pool context.
Profile/direction parameter bytes consumed by projectile setup and movement; the concrete per-field consumers remain open. This label alone is not used to claim coverage of the unknown tail.

Eight kind-indexed offsets used at $B7DC. Projectile state is masked with $07; the selected byte is added to heading $0282,X to form the X/Y movement-table index. These bytes select a motion profile; they are not unknown projectile setup parameters.

Purpose: expand the current area's encoded collision list into fixed six-byte segment records for movement tests
Inputs: area index $A2; concatenated $FF-terminated source lists beginning at $9D8A; line/slope parameters consumed by the compiler and CentralParkMultiply
Outputs: emits endpoint, gradient, flags, and optional-action fields as six-byte records beginning at $FEF9 and writes a zero terminator at the next record
Assumptions: $A2 identifies an existing terminated list and enough RAM is available from $FEF9 upward
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and collision-compiler arithmetic/pointer scratch
Hardware changes: none; writes RAM beneath the KERNAL region under the game's all-RAM banking model

Purpose: compute an unsigned 8-by-8-bit product for collision arithmetic
Inputs: X = unsigned multiplicand; Y = unsigned multiplier
Outputs: Y:X = 16-bit unsigned product
Assumptions: ordinary NMOS 6502 shift/add arithmetic and scratch $45-$47 are available
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and $45-$47
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: test the candidate movement segment against every compiled collision record and report collision plus any encoded trigger
Inputs: X = heading/direction selector; old and candidate coordinates $48-$4B; movement profile $027F; six-byte records beginning at $FEF9
Outputs: returns A=$FF for collision or A=0 for none and restores X from $F3; records the matched record offset in $24; an eligible special segment may set action $80 and OR trigger/collision state into $81
Assumptions: the compiled table is zero-terminated and each nonzero record has the verified six-byte layout
Clobbers: A, Y, flags and collision arithmetic scratch including $23/$24,$45-$47,$F3; X is restored on return
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: invoke sprite composition in the requested masked or collision mode. Inputs: A is mode plus the named compositor's normal actor and frame context. Outputs: composite sprite buffers and metadata are produced. Assumptions: the shared compositor inputs are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and extensive compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Purpose: decode one actor frame descriptor into positioned logical sprite components, temporarily exposing RAM beneath KERNAL for high-memory source data
Inputs: A = frame attribute/modifier; Y = frame-descriptor index; X = first logical-sprite slot; actor state including $70,$72,$7D and frame pointer tables at $C4C2
Outputs: writes component bitmap references, positions, flags, and ready state into logical sprite arrays $0200-$0258 and sets sprite-dirty state as required
Assumptions: frame pointers/descriptors are valid and the caller enters with the normal $01 banking value expected by the matching INC restoration
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and sprite-composition scratch including $F1,$92,$9F
Hardware changes: decrements then restores CPU port $01 to expose high RAM transiently; does not directly write VIC-II sprite registers

Purpose: Enter the Central Park playable phase's common sprite-composition body with the mode already prepared by the masked-mode caller.
Inputs: A/$F1 and $92 contain the prepared composition mode; X selects the logical sprite group; Y selects the frame descriptor; CPU port $01 is in the engine's normal I/O-visible state.
Outputs: Decrements $01 for the required high-memory RAM visibility, resolves and composes the selected frame into logical sprite work buffers, restores $01 before return, and records composition state.
Assumptions: The frame descriptor and phase sprite tables are valid; the routine's balanced DEC/INC of $01 is not interrupted by an alternate exit.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $02/$03, $92/$97/$9F, $F1, and logical sprite work buffers.
Hardware changes: Changes CPU-port $01 transiently by one decrement and a balancing increment to expose the required high-memory RAM; writes sprite work buffers, not VIC-II registers directly.

Purpose: Finish the Central Park playable phase's empty composite-sprite slot by marking its descriptor and restoring CPU-port banking.
Inputs: X selects the logical sprite descriptor at $0218,X; the caller entered with $01 decremented for RAM-under-KERNAL access.
Outputs: Sets bit 6 in $0218,X, increments $01 to restore the caller's banking state, and returns.
Assumptions: This entry is reached only from the empty/no-projectile slot path with one outstanding DEC $01.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, $0218,X, $01, and return-address stack bytes; X and Y are preserved.
Hardware changes: Restores CPU-port $01 banking by one increment; no VIC-II/CIA/SID register write.

Purpose: configure one slot of a composite actor sprite. Inputs: X and Y are part and slot indices and the current part record is valid. Outputs: slot pointer, position, attribute, image, and flip metadata are updated. Assumptions: indices lie within the compositor arrays. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite metadata and RAM only.

Purpose: consume and prepare the next component of a composite sprite definition. Inputs: $02/$03 definition pointer, Y record cursor, and X slot. Outputs: the part is decoded or configured and X and Y advance. Assumptions: the record uses the observed part terminator and encoding. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and part scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: decode a compressed 63-byte sprite and place its part. Inputs: X slot, Y record cursor, and valid compressed-stream context. Outputs: decoded cache and configured part slot are produced. Assumptions: the decoder pointer and part record are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C5/$C6, and decoder and compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: place an already decoded sprite part into the selected composite slot. Inputs: A is preserved across setup, $C5/$C6 hold saved X/Y, and ($02),Y addresses the part record. Outputs: position and attribute arrays are populated and the preserved A is restored by the shared tail. Assumptions: $C5/$C6 and the decoded buffer were prepared by the caller. Clobbers: X, Y, flags, and compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: merge a sprite part into its composite destination under the current mask mode. Inputs: decoded source, destination pointer, placement and flip state, and mode $F1. Outputs: the 63-byte destination sprite region is updated. Assumptions: source and destination each cover the required 63 bytes. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and mask and pointer scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: select the backing buffer for a sprite slot. Inputs: X is sprite-slot index and slot flags are valid. Outputs: the destination pointer is installed in compositor zero page. Assumptions: X lies within the pointer tables. Clobbers: A, flags, and destination pointer; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: merge the cached decoded sprite mask into the active destination. Inputs: $02C0 cache, destination pointer, three masks, and mode $F1. Outputs: the transformed destination sprite bytes are updated. Assumptions: the cache contains a complete decoded sprite. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and mask scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: resolve and expand one tokenized sprite into the fixed 63-byte decode buffer, unless the alternate $C7 mode suppresses decoding
Inputs: A = sprite index; mode byte $C7; split source-pointer tables $CE54/$CF54 plus base $0E54; token stream at resolved $06/$07
Outputs: normal mode fills exactly $02C0-$02FE and returns A=$FF, X=$3F; tokens $69-$6F emit zero runs and $68 escapes a literal; alternate $C7 bit-6 mode adjusts pointer state and returns A=0 without filling the buffer
Assumptions: the sprite index resolves to a valid terminated/length-bounded token stream
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, source pointer $06/$07, and decoder scratch
Hardware changes: none; writes only the 63-byte RAM sprite buffer

Expand a packed sprite into the 63-byte cache $02C0-$02FE from pointer $06/$07. Bytes $69-$6F emit 1-7 zeros; $68 escapes the following byte as one literal, including reserved values. Other bytes are literals. X counts output bytes; Y counts input bytes; return A=$FF. Every one of the 162 main-pool records expands to exactly 63 bytes and consumes precisely the distance to the next record.

Purpose: Resolve the Central Park playable phase's alternate raw sprite pointer without decoding the 63-byte cache.
Inputs: A is the encoded sprite selector and $06 contributes its carried high-address bit; $C7 bit 6 selected raw-pointer mode before this entry.
Outputs: Computes and stores the raw sprite pointer in $06/$07, returns A=0, preserves X, and leaves $02C0-$02FE unchanged.
Assumptions: The encoded selector maps to a valid raw sprite address in the active phase occupant.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, Z, C, and $06/$07; X and the 63-byte cache are preserved.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: update auxiliary sprite or object slot zero. Inputs: slot-zero state at $0280 and shared object and sprite state. Outputs: slot-zero image and position state advance when active and eligible. Assumptions: engine tick and raster gating are active. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and sprite scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM and state only directly.

Purpose: update auxiliary sprite or object slot one. Inputs: slot-one state and shared object and sprite state. Outputs: slot-one image and position state advance when active and eligible. Assumptions: slot layout matches the fixed X=10 and Y=1 mapping. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and sprite scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM and state only directly.

Purpose: Render the Central Park playable phase's auxiliary/projectile sprite slot selected by Y through the common slot-1 body.
Inputs: Y is 0 for slot 0 or 1 for slot 1; $0280,Y and its position/type arrays are current; the caller's rate gate has passed.
Outputs: Returns if the slot is empty; otherwise banks RAM beneath KERNAL, composes the slot into its logical sprite group, restores composition context, and tail-enters scene-condition evaluation.
Assumptions: Y is 0 or 1 and the projectile sprite tables match the active phase.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $C5-$C7, sprite work buffers, and scene-condition scratch.
Hardware changes: Changes CPU-port $01 transiently within the composition helper and restores it before tail transfer; updates sprite work buffers but does not directly write VIC-II registers.

Purpose: Invoke the spatial-object engine for object subtype/channel 0.
Inputs: Current area $A2, player position/heading, object records $C0D0-$C1A2, persistence $03D8+, and event-selected channel.
Outputs: Loads Y=0 and tail-enters CentralParkObjectEngine, which filters matching records and invokes callbacks/draw state.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active, its dispatch tables contain stored return addresses equal to target minus one, and the resident kernel and zero-page gameplay workspace match this phase.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C6, $02/$03, object/animation/draw state, and callback-defined scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Inputs: Y = object mode/channel, stored to $C6; current area $A2; player position/facing; 14-byte records beginning at $C0D0; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y

Purpose: tail-dispatch to the handler selected from an object record. Inputs: $02/$03 is the handler address. Outputs: the handler returns directly to this routine's original caller. Hardware changes: handler-dependent.

Purpose: synchronize and commit object-display state near the bottom raster. Inputs: $A0, tick $E2, object-display pointers $7A/$86, and index $4E. Outputs: display buffers are updated when required and $A0 receives the current or forced-nonzero tick. Assumptions: the undocumented NMOS 6502 opcode span executes with hardware semantics and the indirect pointers are valid. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, indirect destinations, and $A0. Hardware changes: reads VIC-II raster register $D012 and writes hardware-visible display RAM indirectly.

25-byte instruction continuation of $C083, including undocumented LAX absolute,Y at $C096. LAX loads both A/X from the $DC36+Y I/O address; SBC $0486 and CPX $04E4 select paths that execute optional BIT instructions. Every path reaches LDA #4 and stores four through both display pointers $7A/$86 at Y. Four native combinations of comparison operands/carry passed, and LAX A/X matched the stopped CIA timer value for Y=0. The comparisons change the path, not the stored value; exact raster timing and purpose of the comparisons remain open.

End of raster-synchronized object-state update: read the tick $E2, replace zero with $FF, save it as the active-object timestamp $A0, then return. The following $C0B8-$C0CF bytes are a pointer table; they are not instructions.

Six little-endian animation pointers through $C0C3. After object collection, $C062/$C069 compare the active player animation against these candidates using X=10,8,..0; a match replaces it with the parallel pointer at $C0C4/$C0C5 and shifts frame cursor $58 left.
High-byte indexed alias of the six animation words at $C0B8; paired comparisons use even X. This byte does not start a new array.

Six little-endian replacement animation words $C0C4-$C0CF, aligned with the match list at $C0B8. $C06E/$C073 install the matching replacement into $60/$61 and adjust frame cursor; the table is followed by object records.
Odd-byte base of replacement animation pointers beginning $C0C4, selected with the matched even index X. The final word ends at $C0CF.

Purpose: Accept the object callback only when state $0279 equals 7 and then copy the first compiled collision coordinate from $FEF9 to $FEFB.
Inputs: Object-engine callback context and state byte $0279.
Outputs: If $0279==7, copies $FEF9 to $FEFB and returns A=0 so object processing continues; otherwise returns the nonzero state value so the engine skips the record's activation path.
Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active; object record +9/+10 contains this direct callback address, $02/$03 has been loaded from it, and the object engine invokes it through JMP ($02).
Clobbers: A and flags; qualifying path writes $FEFB.
Hardware changes: None directly; the entry changes RAM and/or delegates to gameplay helpers rather than writing C64 I/O registers.

Assumptions: The Central Park PLAY occupant is active; object record +9/+10 contains this direct callback address, $02/$03 has been loaded from it, and the object engine invokes it through JMP ($02).
Clobbers: A and flags; qualifying path writes $03DB/$03DD/$03DE.

Purpose: render each inactive object image belonging to the current Central Park area
Inputs: current area $A2; 14-byte records beginning at $C0D0; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y; inactive scene-record pointer in record bytes 5-6

Purpose: expire a displayed inactive object after 100 engine ticks. Inputs: creation or display tick $A0 and current tick $E2. Outputs: the object remains or is cleared and its UI is refreshed. Purpose: Return from the Central Park playable phase's inactive-object expiry check when the delay has not elapsed or no inactive object is pending.

Purpose: periodically render the alternating active-state image for the first eligible object in the current area
Inputs: timer slot 5; phase counter $A9; current area $A2; 14-byte records at $C0D0; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y; two active scene pointers in record bytes 5-6 and 7-8
Outputs: on an admitted tick decrements $A9, selects one of the two active pointers by $A9 bit 0, loads it into $02/$03, and tail-enters the recursive renderer; clears $A9 and returns when no eligible object remains
Assumptions: area records are ordered, both active pointer fields are either valid or zero, and the timer service is initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $A9, $02/$03, and scene-renderer scratch on a render path
